Alternative#summary.en:
Alternative hypothesis of a test, as in R. Test options also accept unambiguous
abbreviations (`"two"`, `"l"`, `"g"`), like R's `match.arg()`.

AnsariTestOptions.confInt#summary.en: Compute a confidence interval for the ratio of scales and its estimate (R's `conf.int`). Default `false`.

AnsariTestOptions.confLevel#summary.en: Confidence level of the interval. Default `0.95`.

AnsariTestOptions.exact#summary.en:
Exact p-value. Default: exact when both samples have fewer than 50 values and there are no ties. The exact
distribution keeps 2 (m + 1) (floor((m + n + 1)^2 / 4) + 1) doubles and makes m + n passes over half of them;
beyond 2^24 doubles or 2^32 steps (m = n = 203, or m = 1 and n = 2047) it is a RangeError (R computes it however
large).

BartlettTestResult#summary.en: Result of {@link bartlettTest}. Has no `alternative`, as R's `bartlett.test()` returns none.

BartlettTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

BartlettTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

BartlettTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

BartlettTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

BinomCIOptions.method#summary.en:
The interval: `"wilson"` (default), `"wald"`, `"wilsoncc"`, `"agresti-coull"`, `"jeffreys"`,
 `"clopper-pearson"` or `"midp"`. Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted.

BinomCIOptions.sides#summary.en: `"two.sided"` (default), `"left"` (lower limit only) or `"right"` (upper limit only); abbreviations accepted.

BinomDiffCIOptions.method#summary.en:
`"ac"` (Agresti-Caffo, the default), `"wald"`, `"score"` (Newcombe's hybrid score interval), `"mn"`
 (Miettinen-Nurminen) or `"mee"` (Farrington-Manning / Mee). Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted.

BinomDiffCIOptions.sides#summary.en: `"two.sided"` (default), `"left"` (lower limit only) or `"right"` (upper limit only); abbreviations accepted.

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestOptions.alpha#su.en: The level of each one-sided test, in (0, 0.5). Default `0.05`.

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestOptions.margin#s.en: The equivalence margin epsilon, in (0, 1): equivalence means -epsilon < p1 - p2 < epsilon. Required.

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestOptions.method#s.en:
The statistic: `"mn"` (Miettinen-Nurminen score, the default), `"mee"` (Farrington-Manning score) or `"wald"`.
 Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted.

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestResult.alpha#sum.en: The level of each one-sided test.

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestResult.confInt#s.en:
The 1 - 2 alpha interval of p1 - p2 of {@link binomDiffCI} with the same method; equivalence is shown exactly when
 it lies inside (-margin, margin).

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestResult.pValue#su.en: The larger of `pValues`: the p-value of the test of equivalence.

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestResult.pValues#s.en: `[P(Z > z(-margin)), P(Z < z(margin))]`: the one-sided p-values of H01 and H02.

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestResult.result#su.en: `"rejected"` (equivalence shown: both p-values below alpha) or `"not rejected"`, as {@link tost}'s `result`.

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestResult.statistic.en:
`[z(-margin), z(margin)]`, z(delta0) = (p1 - p2 - delta0) / sqrt(var(delta0)): the statistics of H01: p1 - p2 <=
-margin (large values reject) and of H02: p1 - p2 >= margin (small values reject).

BinomDiffEquivalenceTestResult.warnings#.en: Warnings (none: input without a defined result is an error).

BinomRatioCIOptions.method#summary.en: `"katz.log"` (the default) or `"koopman"` (Koopman's score interval). Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted.

BinomRatioCIOptions.sides#summary.en: `"two.sided"` (default), `"left"` (lower limit only) or `"right"` (upper limit only); abbreviations accepted.

BinomTestOptions.confLevel#summary.en: Confidence level of the interval. Default `0.95`.

BinomTestResult.alternative#summary.en: Alternative hypothesis, always in full form.

BinomTestResult.confInt#summary.en: Clopper-Pearson interval for the probability of success.

BinomTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

BinomTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

BinomTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Number of trials (`parameterName` is `"number of trials"`).

BinomTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

BoschlooTestOptions.alternative#summary.en:
Alternative hypothesis, in Exact's orientation: `"less"` means pi1 < pi2 (the proportion of row 1 below that of
row 2). Default `"two.sided"`. Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted.

BoschlooTestOptions.tsmethod#summary.en: Two-sided method: `"square"` (the default, as Exact) or `"central"`. Ignored for one-sided tests.

BoschlooTestResult.alternative#summary.en: Alternative hypothesis, always in full form.

BoschlooTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

BoschlooTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

BoschlooTestResult.nuisanceParameter#sum.en: The common proportion pi under the null hypothesis at which the supremum (the p-value) is attained.

BoschlooTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

BoschlooTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Parameter of the null distribution of the statistic, such as degrees of freedom (R's `parameter`).

BoschlooTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

BoschlooTsMethod#summary.en:
Two-sided method of {@link boschlooTest}: `"square"` (Boschloo's original: Fisher's two-sided p-value as the
statistic) or `"central"` (twice the one-sided p-value in the direction of the data).

BrunnerMunzelTestOptions.alternative#sum.en:
Alternative hypothesis (unambiguous abbreviations accepted). Default `"two.sided"`. As in lawstat, `"greater"`
means that `x` tends to be larger than `y` (the relative effect is below 1/2) and `"less"` the opposite.

BrunnerMunzelTestOptions.confLevel#summa.en: Confidence level of the interval for the relative effect (lawstat's `1 - alpha`). Default `0.95`.

CISides#summary.en:
Which limits of a proportion's interval are kept (DescTools' `sides`): `"two.sided"` both, `"left"` the lower one
(the upper is the end of the range), `"right"` the upper one.

ChisqStatTestResult#summary.en: Result of a k-sample test with a chi-squared statistic. Has no `alternative`, as R returns none.

ChisqStatTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

ChisqStatTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

ChisqStatTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

ChisqStatTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

ChisqTestFactorsResult#summary.en: Result of {@link chisqTest} with two factor vectors: also the levels that label the rows and columns.

ChisqTestFactorsResult.colLevels#summary.en: Levels of `y` (columns of the table), sorted by code point.

ChisqTestFactorsResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

ChisqTestFactorsResult.expected#summary.en: Expected counts under the null hypothesis.

ChisqTestFactorsResult.ftResiduals#summa.en:
Freeman-Tukey deviates `sqrt(O) + sqrt(O + 1) - sqrt(4E + 1)` (Bishop, Fienberg and Holland 1975; not in R),
approximately standard normal under the null hypothesis; their sum of squares is the Freeman-Tukey statistic.

ChisqTestFactorsResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

ChisqTestFactorsResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

ChisqTestFactorsResult.observed#summary.en: Observed counts (an array of rows for a contingency table).

ChisqTestFactorsResult.rowLevels#summary.en: Levels of `x` (rows of the table), sorted by code point.

ChisqTestFactorsResult.stdres#summary.en:
Standardized residuals `(O - E) / sqrt(V)`, where `V` is
`E (1 - row proportion) (1 - column proportion)` for a contingency table and
`n p (1 - p)` for goodness of fit. For a contingency table the complements are the other rows' and columns'
sums over the total, and the residual and `V` are computed in double-double.

ChisqTestFactorsResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

ChisqTestOptions.correct#summary.en: Apply Yates' continuity correction (2 x 2 tables only). Default `true`.

ChisqTestOptions.nMinus1#summary.en:
The 'N - 1' chi-squared test (Campbell 2007; not in R): Pearson's statistic times `(N - 1) / N`, without continuity
correction, for a contingency table (2 x 2 or larger). Default `false`. An error for goodness of fit (a vector or
a matrix with one row or column), with `simulatePValue`, and with `correct: true` given explicitly (the default
correction is not applied).

ChisqTestOptions.p#summary.en: Expected probabilities for the goodness-of-fit test. Default: equal probabilities. Ignored for contingency tables.

ChisqTestOptions.rescaleP#summary.en: Rescale `p` to sum to 1. Default `false`, in which case `p` must sum to 1.

ChisqTestOptions.simulatePValue#summary.en:
Compute the p-value by Monte Carlo simulation with `B` replicates (R's `simulate.p.value`), using the random
stream of {@link setSeed} as R does. Default `false`.

ChisqTestResult#summary.en: Result of {@link chisqTest}. Has no `alternative`, because R's `chisq.test()` does not return one.

ChisqTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

ChisqTestResult.expected#summary.en: Expected counts under the null hypothesis.

ChisqTestResult.ftResiduals#summary.en:
Freeman-Tukey deviates `sqrt(O) + sqrt(O + 1) - sqrt(4E + 1)` (Bishop, Fienberg and Holland 1975; not in R),
approximately standard normal under the null hypothesis; their sum of squares is the Freeman-Tukey statistic.

ChisqTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

ChisqTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

ChisqTestResult.observed#summary.en: Observed counts (an array of rows for a contingency table).

ChisqTestResult.stdres#summary.en:
Standardized residuals `(O - E) / sqrt(V)`, where `V` is
`E (1 - row proportion) (1 - column proportion)` for a contingency table and
`n p (1 - p)` for goodness of fit. For a contingency table the complements are the other rows' and columns'
sums over the total, and the residual and `V` are computed in double-double.

ChisqTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

CorOptions#summary.en:
The base of {@link CorTestOptions}: the options {@link corTest} shares with the coefficient. The options of the
exported `cor` (descriptive statistics) are {@link CovOptions}.

CorOptions.method#summary.en: Correlation coefficient to compute. Default `"pearson"`. Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted.

CorTestOptions.alternative#summary.en:
Alternative hypothesis: `"two.sided"`, `"less"` or `"greater"`. Default `"two.sided"`.
Unambiguous abbreviations such as `"two"`, `"l"` and `"g"` are accepted, as in R.

CorTestOptions.confLevel#summary.en: Confidence level of the interval (Pearson only; the interval needs at least 4 pairs). Default `0.95`.

CorTestOptions.continuity#summary.en: Apply a continuity correction when the approximation is used (Kendall and Spearman). Default `false`.

CorTestOptions.exact#summary.en:
Compute an exact p-value (Kendall and Spearman). Default: as in R, exact when there are
no ties and n < 50 (Kendall) or n <= 1290 (Spearman). With ties the approximation is
always used. Kendall's exact distribution takes about n^3 / 2 steps: for n above 1290 (about 5 s)
`exact: true` without ties is a RangeError (R computes it however long it takes).

CorTestOptions.method#summary.en: Correlation coefficient to compute. Default `"pearson"`. Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted.

CorTestResult#summary.en:
Result of {@link corTest}. For Pearson, `statisticName` is `"t"` with `parameter` (df)
and `confInt`; for Kendall `"T"` (exact) or `"z"`; for Spearman `"S"`.

CorTestResult.alternative#summary.en: Alternative hypothesis, always in full form.

CorTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

CorTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Correlation under the null hypothesis: always `0`.

CorTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Parameter of the null distribution of the statistic, such as degrees of freedom (R's `parameter`).

CorTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

Counts#summary.en: Counts: an array of numbers. A contingency table is passed as an array of rows.

CvmTestResult#summary.en: Result of {@link cvmTest}, with nortest's warning for a p-value below the approximation's range.

CvmTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

CvmTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

CvmTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

CvmTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Parameter of the null distribution of the statistic, such as degrees of freedom (R's `parameter`).

CvmTestResult.warnings#summary.en: Warnings, as nortest gives them (empty when there are none).

Factor#summary.en: A factor: category labels, with `null` or `undefined` for missing values (R's NA).

FisherTestOptions.alternative#summary.en:
Alternative hypothesis: `"two.sided"`, `"less"` or `"greater"`. Default `"two.sided"`.
Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted. Used for 2 x 2 tables only.

FisherTestOptions.confInt#summary.en: Compute a confidence interval for the odds ratio (2 x 2 tables only). Default `true`.

FisherTestOptions.confLevel#summary.en: Confidence level of the interval (2 x 2 tables only). Default `0.95`.

FisherTestOptions.midp#summary.en:
The mid-p version of the test of a 2 x 2 table (as `exact2x2::fisher.exact(x, midp = TRUE)`): the p-value and the
confidence limits from the mid-p tails P(X < x) + P(X = x)/2 and P(X > x) + P(X = x)/2 of the (1, 1) cell; the
two-sided p-value is twice the smaller tail (the central test) and the estimate stays the conditional MLE. An error
for larger tables. Default `false`.

FisherTestOptions.or#summary.en: Odds ratio under the null hypothesis (2 x 2 tables only). Default `1`.

FisherTestOptions.simulatePValue#summary.en:
Compute the p-value of an r x c table (larger than 2 x 2) by Monte Carlo simulation with `B` replicates (R's
`simulate.p.value`), using the random stream of {@link setSeed} as R does. Ignored for 2 x 2 tables. Default
`false`.

FisherTestResult#summary.en:
Result of {@link fisherTest}. Has no `statistic` or `statisticName`, because R's
`fisher.test()` does not return a statistic. For 2 x 2 tables, `estimate` is the
conditional maximum likelihood estimate of the odds ratio and `confInt` its interval;
for larger tables only `method`, `alternative` and `pValue` are set.

FisherTestResult.alternative#summary.en: Alternative hypothesis, always in full form.

FisherTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

FisherTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

FisherTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

FisherTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Parameter of the null distribution of the statistic, such as degrees of freedom (R's `parameter`).

FisherTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

GTestOptions.correct#summary.en:
`"none"` (default), `"williams"` (Williams' correction q of the statistic) or `"yates"` (Yates' correction of the
counts by 0.5, 2 x 2 tables and two-category goodness of fit only). Unambiguous abbreviations are accepted.

GTestOptions.p#summary.en: Expected probabilities for the goodness-of-fit test. Default: equal probabilities. Ignored for a table.

GTestOptions.rescaleP#summary.en: Rescale `p` to sum to 1. Default `false`, in which case `p` must sum to 1 (within sqrt(eps)).

GTestResult#summary.en: Result of {@link gTest}. Has no `alternative`, as DescTools' `GTest` returns none.

GTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

GTestResult.expected#summary.en: Expected counts under the null hypothesis.

GTestResult.ftResiduals#summary.en:
Freeman-Tukey deviates `sqrt(O) + sqrt(O + 1) - sqrt(4E + 1)` of the counts given (without Yates' correction),
approximately standard normal under the null hypothesis.

GTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

GTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

GTestResult.observed#summary.en: The counts, after Yates' correction where it is applied (as DescTools); an array of rows for a table.

GTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Degrees of freedom (`parameterName` is `"X-squared df"`, as DescTools).

GTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

GoodmanKruskalGammaResult.ase#summary.en: The asymptotic standard error ASE1 (not under the null hypothesis).

GoodmanKruskalGammaResult.confInt#summar.en: The Wald interval `gamma -/+ z ase`, clipped to [-1, 1].

GoodmanKruskalGammaResult.estimate#summa.en: Gamma, `(C - D) / (C + D)` with C and D the numbers of concordant and discordant pairs (NaN when both are 0).

GroupLabel#summary.en: Group label: a number or a string.

HTest#summary.en:
Result of a hypothesis test: a plain object mirroring R's `htest` class.

R's named values (`statistic`, `parameter`, `estimate`, `null.value`) are split into a
number and a separate `...Name` field. `estimate` is an array only when there are two
estimates (for example the two means of a two-sample t-test). `conf.int`'s
`conf.level` attribute becomes `confLevel`.

HTest.alternative#summary.en: Alternative hypothesis, always in full form.

HTest.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

HTest.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

HTest.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

HTest.parameter#summary.en: Parameter of the null distribution of the statistic, such as degrees of freedom (R's `parameter`).

HTest.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

JonckheereTestOptions.exact#summary.en:
The exact p-value (`"DescTools"` only). Default: exact when there are no ties and at most 100 observations. With
ties the normal approximation is used anyway, with a warning. The exact distribution is the convolution of the
Mann-Whitney distributions; where it would have more than 2^24 values or take more than 2^32 multiply-adds
(three groups of 215, about 8 s), `exact: true` is a RangeError (R computes it however long it takes).

JonckheereTestOptions.levels#summary.en: The order of the groups. Default: the labels sorted (numbers as numbers, strings by code point).

JonckheereTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

JonckheereTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

JonckheereTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

JonckheereTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Parameter of the null distribution of the statistic, such as degrees of freedom (R's `parameter`).

KsTestOptions.alternative#summary.en:
Alternative hypothesis (unambiguous abbreviations accepted). `"greater"`: the distribution function of `x` lies
above that of `y` (statistic D^+); `"less"`: below (D^-). Default `"two.sided"`.

KsTestOptions.exact#summary.en:
Exact p-value. Default: exact for one sample of fewer than 100 values without ties, and for two samples with
m n < 10000. The exact two-sided one-sample p-value for D < 1/2 raises a matrix of size 2 floor(n D) + 1 to the
n-th power; where that needs more than 2^33 multiply-adds (m 781 at n 1023, about 4 s) it is a RangeError (R
computes it however long it takes).

KsTestResult#summary.en:
Result of {@link ksTest}. As in R, `alternative` describes the hypothesis in words ("two-sided", "the CDF of x lies
above the null hypothesis", ...), and `exact` tells whether the p-value is exact.

KsTestResult.alternative#summary.en: Description of the alternative hypothesis, as R prints it (e.g. `"two-sided"`).

KsTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

KsTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

KsTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

KsTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Parameter of the null distribution of the statistic, such as degrees of freedom (R's `parameter`).

KsTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

LblTestOptions.colScores#summary.en: Scores of the columns. Default `1, 2, ..., c`.

LblTestOptions.rowScores#summary.en: Scores of the rows. Default `1, 2, ..., r`.

LeveneTestOptions.center#summary.en: The centre of each group: `"median"` (default) or `"mean"`.

LeveneTestResult.table#summary.en: One array per row; NaN where car prints nothing.

LeveneTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

MantelhaenTestOptions.alternative#summar.en: Alternative hypothesis (2 x 2 x K only). Default `"two.sided"`.

MantelhaenTestOptions.confLevel#summary.en: Confidence level of the interval for the common odds ratio. Default `0.95`.

MantelhaenTestOptions.correct#summary.en: Continuity correction (2 x 2 x K, asymptotic test). Default `true`.

MantelhaenTestOptions.exact#summary.en: Exact conditional test (2 x 2 x K). Default `false`.

MantelhaenTestResult#summary.en: Result of {@link mantelhaenTest}. 2 x 2 x K tables add the common odds ratio and its interval.

MantelhaenTestResult.alternative#summary.en: Present for 2 x 2 x K tables.

MantelhaenTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

MantelhaenTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

MantelhaenTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

MantelhaenTestResult.parameter#summary.en: Parameter of the null distribution of the statistic, such as degrees of freedom (R's `parameter`).

MantelhaenTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

McnemarTestOptions.correct#summary.en: Apply the continuity correction (2 x 2 tables only). Default `true`.

McnemarTestResult#summary.en: Result of {@link mcnemarTest}. Has no `alternative`, as R's `mcnemar.test()` returns none.

McnemarTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

McnemarTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

McnemarTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

McnemarTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

NormalityTestResult#summary.en: Result of a normality test: no `alternative`, as nortest returns none.

OddsRatioOptions.method#summary.en:
`"midp"` (the default: median-unbiased estimate and mid-p exact interval), `"fisher"` (conditional MLE and
 Fisher's exact interval), `"wald"` or `"score"` (epiR's score interval). Unambiguous abbreviations accepted.

OddsRatioResult.estimate#summary.en:
The odds ratio: the median-unbiased estimate (`"midp"`), the conditional MLE (`"fisher"`) or the sample odds
 ratio x11 x22 / (x12 x21) (`"wald"`, `"score"`).

OddsRatioResult.method#summary.en: epitools' description of the method (e.g. `"median-unbiased estimate & mid-p exact CI"`).

OddsRatioResult.pValue#summary.en: epitools' p-values of independence, the same for every method.

OddsRatioResult.pValue.chiSquare#summary.en: Pearson's chi-squared test without continuity correction.

OddsRatioResult.pValue.midp#summary.en: The two-sided mid-p exact p-value: twice the smaller one-sided mid-p value P(X < a) + P(X = a)/2.

OddsRatioResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings ("Chi-squared approximation may be incorrect" where an expected count is below 5).

OnewayTestOptions.varEqual#summary.en: Assume equal variances (the classical F test). Default `false` (Welch's test).

OnewayTestResult#summary.en: Result of {@link onewayTest}: an F statistic with two degrees of freedom.

OnewayTestResult.estimate#summary.en: Estimate(s) of the parameter being tested (R's `estimate`).

OnewayTestResult.method#summary.en: Description of the test, as R's `method` (e.g. `"Welch Two Sample t-test"`).

OnewayTestResult.nullValue#summary.en: Value of the parameter under the null hypothesis (R's `null.value`).

OnewayTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

PearsonTestOptions.adjust#summary.en: Subtract the 2 estimated parameters from the degrees of freedom. Default `true`.

interval's search meets. Where that would take more than about 8 seconds, a RangeError suggesting `exact: false`
is thrown before the computation. Measured on a Mac mini (Apple M1, Node 24) with data rounded to one or two
decimals: the p-value up to about n = 2400 (one sample) and m = n = 320 (two samples); the interval up to about
n = 150 to 300 (one sample; 4 s at n = 150 with 3 decimals, 4.6 s at n = 300 with 1) and m = n = 80 (two samples;

warnings R gives before it stops.

binomCI#summary.en:
Confidence interval for a binomial proportion x/n. Equivalent to `DescTools::BinomCI()` in R.

Methods (`method`): `"wilson"` (the default, Wilson's score interval), `"wald"`, `"wilsoncc"` (with continuity
correction), `"agresti-coull"`, `"jeffreys"`, `"clopper-pearson"` (the exact interval) and `"midp"` (the mid-p exact
interval). With `sides: "left"` or `"right"` only the lower or the upper limit is kept, at the one-sided level
`confLevel` (the two-sided interval at `1 - 2 (1 - confLevel)`), and the other end is 0 or 1. Limits are clipped to
[0, 1].

The mid-p limits are the roots of their equations to the precision of the doubles; DescTools stops its search at
an absolute 1.22e-4, which leaves its limits up to 1e-4 off and gives 0 for lower limits below that. Unlike
DescTools, which returns NaN or numbers, x > n, a negative or non-integer count, n = 0 and a level outside (0, 1)
are errors.

RangeError for counts that are not integers with 0 <= x <= n, n > 0, a level outside (0, 1) (at least 0.5

binomDiffCI#summary.en:
Confidence interval for the difference p1 - p2 of two independent proportions x1/n1 and x2/n2. Equivalent to
`DescTools::BinomDiffCI()` in R.

Methods (`method`): `"ac"` (Agresti-Caffo, the default as in DescTools: the Wald interval with one success and one
failure added to each group), `"wald"`, `"score"` (Newcombe's hybrid score interval, his method 10), `"mn"`
(Miettinen-Nurminen score interval) and `"mee"` (Farrington-Manning / Mee: the same without the factor N/(N - 1);
epiR's score interval of the attributable risk). With `sides: "left"` or `"right"` only the lower or the upper limit
is kept, at the one-sided level `confLevel`, and the other end is 1 or -1. The `"mn"` and `"mee"` limits are the
roots of the score statistic to the precision of the doubles (DescTools stops at about 1e-7 and 1e-4).

binomDiffEquivalenceTest#@throws.en:
RangeError for counts that are not integers with 0 <= x <= n, n > 0, a margin outside (0, 1), alpha
  outside (0, 0.5), or an unknown method.

binomDiffEquivalenceTest#summary.en:
Test of equivalence of two independent proportions x1/n1 and x2/n2 within a margin. Two one-sided tests of
H01: p1 - p2 <= -margin and H02: p1 - p2 >= margin, each at level `alpha`; equivalence is shown when both reject.
Not an R function. (The R packages in scope give the dual intervals, `DescTools::BinomDiffCI`, or test one bound at
a time.)

The statistic at a bound delta0 is z = (p1 - p2 - delta0) / sqrt(var), with var the variance of p1 - p2 at the
maximum likelihood estimate of (p1, p2) under p1 - p2 = delta0 (Farrington and Manning 1990, `"mee"`), the same times
N/(N - 1) (Miettinen and Nurminen 1985, `"mn"`, the default), or at the observed proportions (`"wald"`). The
p-values are normal tails. The test is dual to {@link binomDiffCI} with the same method at the level 1 - 2 alpha:
equivalence is shown exactly when that interval, returned as `confInt`, lies inside (-margin, margin).

The Wald variance is 0 when both proportions are 0 or 1: the statistics are then infinite and the p-values 0 or 1,
as binomDiffCI's Wald interval is a point there.

binomRatioCI#summary.en:
Confidence interval for the ratio p1/p2 of two independent proportions x1/n1 and x2/n2 (the risk ratio). Equivalent
to `DescTools::BinomRatioCI()` in R.

Methods (`method`): `"katz.log"` (the default; Katz's log interval, with 0.5 put for a zero count, and n - 0.5 for
both counts when both groups are all successes, as DescTools) and `"koopman"` (Koopman's score interval, also epiR's
score interval of the risk ratio), whose limits are the roots of Koopman's statistic to the precision of the
doubles. With `sides: "left"` or `"right"` only the lower or the upper limit is kept, at the one-sided level
`confLevel`, and the other end is Infinity or 0 (DescTools computes the one-sided level but keeps both limits).
With x1 = x2 = 0 the estimate is 0 and the interval [0, Infinity], as DescTools.

boschlooTest#@param table.en: A 2 x 2 table of counts: rows are the groups, column 1 the events.

boschlooTest#summary.en:
Boschloo's exact unconditional test (`method = "boschloo"`) for a 2 x 2 table whose rows are two independent
binomial samples. Equivalent to `Exact::exact.test()` in R.

The rows are the groups and column 1 counts the events: `[[x1, n1 - x1], [x2, n2 - x2]]`. The statistic is Fisher's
exact p-value of each possible table (one-sided, or two-sided for `tsmethod: "square"`), and the p-value is the
largest probability, over the common proportion pi under the null hypothesis, of the tables whose statistic is at
most the observed one (Boschloo 1970). `alternative: "less"` means pi1 < pi2 (Exact's orientation; exact2x2's
`boschloo()` uses the opposite one). `"central"` doubles the one-sided p-value in the direction of the data.

The p-value is the true supremum, from a fine grid and a refinement of every candidate maximum; Exact maximises
over 100 points refined by `optimise` and rounds to 12 digits (about 1e-9 relative off), and its two-sided
`"square"` region can contain tables that do not belong there (docs/differences-from-r.md). `statistic` is the
observed Fisher p-value (one-sided in the direction tested, or two-sided for `"square"`), `estimate` the difference
of the proportions x1/n1 - x2/n2, and `nuisanceParameter` the pi at which the supremum is attained.

A table with more than 2^24 possible outcomes ((n1 + 1)(n2 + 1)) is a RangeError, as is one whose grid would take
more than about 10 seconds.

brunnerMunzelTest#summary.en:
Brunner-Munzel test that two samples have the relative effect P(X < Y) + P(X = Y)/2 = 1/2, without assuming equal
variances or shapes. Equivalent to `lawstat::brunner.munzel.test()` in R. `NaN` values are dropped.

`estimate` is the estimated relative effect and `confInt` its two-sided interval (not clipped to [0, 1]). Each
sample needs at least 2 values (lawstat returns NaN for a sample of one). When the variance estimates are 0 (for
example completely separated samples), the statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value are `NaN` or ±Infinity, as in
lawstat.

chisqTest(0)#summary.en:
Pearson's chi-squared test. Equivalent to R's `chisq.test()`.

Given an array of counts, tests goodness of fit to `options.p`. Given a matrix (an array
of rows), tests independence in the contingency table; a matrix with a single row or
column is treated as a goodness-of-fit test, as in R. Yates' correction is applied to
2 x 2 tables by default; as in R, the amount subtracted is `min(0.5, min |O - E|)` over
all cells. Sums are computed in extended precision, like R.

With `simulatePValue: true` the p-value is computed from `B` simulated samples (multinomial for goodness of fit,
random tables with the observed margins otherwise), drawn from the random stream of {@link setSeed} exactly as in
R, so `setSeed(s)` before the call gives R's p-value after `set.seed(s)`.

Given two factor vectors (arrays of labels of the same length), tests independence in their contingency table, as
R's `chisq.test(x, y)`; pairs with a missing label are dropped and the levels are sorted by code point.

With `nMinus1: true` (not in R) the statistic is Campbell's (2007) 'N - 1' chi-squared, Pearson's statistic without
continuity correction times `(N - 1) / N`, for 2 x 2 and larger tables with a total N above 1. The result also has
the Freeman-Tukey deviates `ftResiduals` (not in R).

As R, `warnings` has "Chi-squared approximation may be incorrect" where an expected count is below 5 (unless the
p-value is simulated), and "cannot compute simulated p-value with zero marginals" where `simulatePValue` is asked for
a table with a zero row or column sum (the ordinary test is done).

corTest(0)#summary.en:
Test for correlation between paired samples. Equivalent to R's `cor.test()`.

Supports Pearson's product-moment correlation (t test, with a Fisher-z confidence
interval), Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho (exact or approximate p-values, chosen by
the same rules as R). Pairs containing `NaN` are dropped; Pearson needs at least 3
pairs and the others at least 2. If the correlation is undefined (constant data) the
statistic, p-value and estimate are `NaN`. Correlations are computed in double-double
arithmetic, so results can differ from R's when r is very close to ±1, where R's own
value is less accurate.

As R, `warnings` has "the standard deviation is zero" where x or y is constant (the correlation is `NaN`), and
"cannot compute exact p-value with ties" (R 4.6's text) where Kendall's or Spearman's exact p-value is asked for or
the default but there are ties (the approximation is used), and "NaNs produced" where Spearman's t approximation has 2 pairs
(0 degrees of freedom: the p-value is `NaN`).

formula `"~ x + y"` names the two variables. Only they count: the rows where one of them is missing are dropped.

cvmTest#summary.en:
Cramer-von Mises test for normality. Equivalent to `nortest::cvm.test()` in R. `NaN` values are dropped; at least 8
values are needed.

fisherTest#@param x.en: Contingency table as an array of rows (at least 2 x 2).

fisherTest#summary.en:
Fisher's exact test for count data. Equivalent to R's `fisher.test()`.

Tests independence in an r x c contingency table with fixed margins. For 2 x 2 tables
it also returns the conditional MLE of the odds ratio and its confidence interval,
reproducing R's numbers (including R's root-finding tolerance). The two-sided p-value
sums the probabilities of tables no more likely than the observed one (relative
tolerance `1e-7`, as in R). Non-integer counts are rounded to the nearest integer
(ties to even), with R's warning ("'x' has been rounded to integer: Mean relative difference: 0.0625", the text of
R's `all.equal` of the counts and the rounded counts; none where they differ by less than about 1.5e-8).

With `simulatePValue: true`, the p-value of a table larger than 2 x 2 is computed from `B` random tables with the
observed margins, drawn from the random stream of {@link setSeed} exactly as in R.

With `midp: true` (2 x 2 only), the mid-p version of exact2x2's `fisher.exact()`: the p-value and the interval come
from the mid-p tails (two-sided: the central test, twice the smaller tail, at most 1), the limits are the roots of
the mid-p tails to the precision of the doubles (exact2x2's search stops up to 1% from them), and `method` is
`"Central Fisher's Exact Test (mid-p version)"` or `"One-sided Fisher's Exact Test (mid-p version)"`.

Not implemented: R's `hybrid` option.

flignerTest(0)#@param g.en:
Group labels, parallel to `x`.

There is also a formula form, `flignerTest("y ~ g", data)` (next overload).

flignerTest(0)#@param x.en:
An array of samples (each with at least one non-missing value, as R requires), or one sample with group
  labels `g`.

flignerTest(0)#summary.en: Fligner-Killeen (median) test of homogeneity of variances. Equivalent to R's `fligner.test()`.

flignerTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

flignerTest(1)#summary.en:
Fligner-Killeen test from a formula and a data frame. As R's `fligner.test(formula, data)`: `"y ~ g"`,
one group per level of `g`. Only the variables of the formula count: the rows where one of them is missing are
dropped.

friedmanTest(0)#@param y.en:
Blocks as rows, treatments as columns. Rows with a missing value are dropped.

There is also a formula form, `friedmanTest("y ~ w | b", data)` (next overload).

friedmanTest(0)#summary.en:
Friedman rank sum test for an unreplicated complete block design. Equivalent to R's `friedman.test()`. Takes a
matrix.

friedmanTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

friedmanTest(1)#@param formula.en: `"y ~ w | b"` (one variable on each side of `|`).

friedmanTest(1)#summary.en:
Friedman test from a formula and a data frame. As R's `friedman.test(formula, data)`: `"y ~ w | b"`
with the groups `w` and the blocks `b`. The rows where `y`, `w` or `b` is missing are dropped first; then every
combination of group and block must occur exactly once (else the error `not an unreplicated complete block
design`, so that one missing value fails, unlike the matrix form, which drops its block).

gTest#@param x.en: Counts (nonnegative, finite; not all 0), or a contingency table as an array of rows.

gTest#@returns.en: The test result, with `statisticName` `"G"`; see {@link GTestResult}.

gTest#@throws.en:
RangeError for negative or non-finite counts, a total of 0, fewer than 2 counts, `p` of the wrong length,
  negative or not summing to 1, `"yates"` for anything but a 2 x 2 table or two counts, and `"williams"` for a
  table with an empty row or column.

gTest#summary.en:
Log-likelihood ratio (G) test of independence in a contingency table, or of goodness of fit of counts to given
probabilities. Equivalent to `DescTools::GTest()` in R.

For a table (an array of rows), `G = 2 sum x log(x / E) / q` with `E` the products of the margins over the total and
`(r - 1)(c - 1)` degrees of freedom, counting empty rows and columns as DescTools; for a vector (or a table with one
row or column), `E = n p` and `k - 1` degrees of freedom. `correct: "williams"` divides by Williams' q
(`1 + (n sum 1/R_i - 1)(n sum 1/C_j - 1) / (6 n (r - 1)(c - 1))` for a table, which is not defined with an empty
row or column: an error, where DescTools gives G = 0 and p = 1; and `1 + (k + 1) / (6n)` for a vector). `correct: "yates"` moves the counts of a 2 x 2 table by 0.5 toward
independence as DescTools does: the off-diagonal cells up and the diagonal down when `x11 x22 - x12 x21 > 0`, and
the other way otherwise, also when it is 0 (so that a table of exact independence gets a positive G), and without
stopping at 0 (a cell that becomes negative makes G NaN, with the warning "NaNs produced"). For two counts it moves
them by 0.5 toward `E` when they differ from it by more than 0.25.

The p-value is the upper tail of chi-squared (DescTools computes `1 - pchisq` for a table, which is 0 below about
1e-16). G is summed as a deviance, without the cancellation of the plain sum. The result also has the Freeman-Tukey
deviates `ftResiduals`.

goodmanKruskalGamma#@param table.en: A table of counts (nonnegative, finite) as an array of rows; rows and columns in their order.

goodmanKruskalGamma#@throws.en: RangeError for negative or non-finite counts, or a level outside (0, 1).

goodmanKruskalGamma#summary.en:
Goodman and Kruskal's gamma of a table of two ordered classifications, with its asymptotic standard error and a
Wald confidence interval. Equivalent to `DescTools::GoodmanKruskalGamma()` in R.

`gamma = (C - D) / (C + D)` with C and D the numbers of concordant and discordant pairs. The standard error is the
non-null ASE1 (Agresti 2010, section 7.1): `sqrt(sum x psi^2)` with `psi_ij = 2 (D Pc_ij - C Pd_ij) / (C + D)^2`,
`Pc_ij` the counts above-left and below-right of cell (i, j) and `Pd_ij` those above-right and below-left. The
interval is `[max(-1, gamma - z ase), min(1, gamma + z ase)]`, z the normal quantile of `1 - (1 - confLevel) / 2`.
Without concordant or discordant pairs (a table with one row, for example) gamma and the interval are NaN, as
DescTools. No test of gamma = 0 is given (it would need the null standard error).

jonckheereTest#@param g.en: Group labels, parallel to `x`, in the order of the alternative.

jonckheereTest#summary.en:
Jonckheere-Terpstra test of equal distributions against ordered alternatives. Equivalent to
`DescTools::JonckheereTerpstraTest()` in R. Computes `JonckheereTerpstraTest(x, g, alternative, exact)` (with `g`
an ordered factor) or, with `variant: "clinfun"`, clinfun's `jonckheere.test(x, g, alternative)` (whose
two-sided p-value is `2 min(p_increasing, p_decreasing, 0.5)`; DescTools caps it at 1 instead of 0.5). Pairs with a missing value are dropped (with `variant: "clinfun"`, also those with an infinite value, as clinfun does).

kruskalTest(0)#@param g.en:
Group labels, parallel to `x`.

There is also a formula form, `kruskalTest("y ~ g", data)` (next overload).

kruskalTest(0)#@param x.en:
An array of samples (each with at least one non-missing value, as R requires), or one sample with group
  labels `g`.

kruskalTest(0)#summary.en: Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test. Equivalent to R's `kruskal.test()`.

kruskalTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

kruskalTest(1)#summary.en:
Kruskal-Wallis test from a formula and a data frame. As R's `kruskal.test(formula, data)`: `"y ~ g"`,
one group per level of `g`. Only the variables of the formula count: the rows where one of them is missing are
dropped.

ksTest(0)#@param options.en:
See {@link KsTestOptions}.

There is also a formula form for two samples, `ksTest("y ~ g", data, options)` (next overload).

ksTest(0)#@param y.en: A continuous distribution function, or a second sample.

ksTest(0)#summary.en:
Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Equivalent to R's `ks.test()`. Takes a distribution function given as a function (for
example `(q) => pnorm(q)`) or a second sample. `NaN` values are dropped.

As R, `warnings` has "ties should not be present for the one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test" for one sample with
ties, and "p-value will be approximate in the presence of ties" for two samples with ties and `exact: false` (or
m n >= 10000).

ksTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

ksTest(1)#summary.en:
Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test from a formula and a data frame. As R's `ks.test(formula, data)`:
`"y ~ g"` compares the two levels of `g` (the first level is `x`). Only the variables of the formula count: the
rows where one of them is missing are dropped.

lblTest#@param table.en: A table of counts (nonnegative, finite) as an array of rows.

lblTest#@returns.en: The test result, with `statisticName` `"Z"`; see {@link LblTestResult}.

lblTest#@throws.en:
RangeError for negative or non-finite counts, a total of at most 1, scores of the wrong length or not
  finite, and tables whose row or column scores do not vary over the observations (Z undefined).

lblTest#summary.en:
Asymptotic linear-by-linear association test of a table of two ordered classifications (the Mantel test of trend).
Equivalent to `coin::lbl_test()` in R. As coin's asymptotic test, except for tables with a two-level factor.

`Z = sqrt(N - 1) r`, r the Pearson correlation of the row and column scores over the N observations: the linear
statistic `sum x_ij u_i v_j` standardised by its permutation (conditional) mean and variance. The scores are 1..k
by default for every factor (the level index; empty rows and columns keep their place). coin leaves a two-level
factor unordered and codes it by an indicator of its first level, which turns the sign of Z, and refuses 2 x 2
tables; here two-level factors are scored like the others and a 2 x 2 table is tested (Z^2 is then the 'N - 1'
chi-squared statistic). p-values from the normal distribution: `"greater"` is positive association.

leveneTest#summary.en:
Levene's test for homogeneity of variance across groups. Equivalent to `car::leveneTest()` in R. Computes
`leveneTest(y ~ g, center = median)` (or `mean`). Pairs with a missing value are dropped; groups are ordered by
their sorted labels.

lillieTest#summary.en:
Lilliefors (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) test for normality. Equivalent to `nortest::lillie.test()` in R. `NaN` values are
dropped; at least 5 values are needed.

mantelhaenTest#@param strata.en:
The K strata, each an I x J table of counts as an array of rows (all of the same shape; I, J >= 2,
  K >= 2 for the asymptotic test).

mantelhaenTest#summary.en:
Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel chi-squared test of conditional independence in a set of contingency tables, one per
stratum. Equivalent to R's `mantelhaen.test()`. Takes the strata as R takes a three-dimensional array.

mcnemarTest#@param x.en: Square table of counts as an array of rows, or the first of two paired samples of category codes.

mcnemarTest#@param y.en:
Second paired sample of category codes, when `x` is a sample. May be omitted (and the options passed in
  its place) when `x` is a table.

mcnemarTest#summary.en:
McNemar's chi-squared test for symmetry of rows and columns in a square table of counts. Equivalent to R's
`mcnemar.test()`. Takes a matrix, or two factors given as paired category codes.

moodTest(0)#summary.en:
Mood's two-sample test of scale. Equivalent to R's `mood.test()`. `NaN` values are dropped; ties get the average
of the scores of their positions.

There is also a formula form, `moodTest("y ~ g", data, options)` (next overload).

moodTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

moodTest(1)#summary.en:
Mood's test from a formula and a data frame. As R's `mood.test(formula, data)`: `"y ~ g"` compares the
two levels of `g` (the first level is `x`). Only the variables of the formula count: the rows where one of them is
missing are dropped.

oddsRatio#@param table.en: A 2 x 2 table of counts as an array of rows.

oddsRatio#@returns.en:
See {@link OddsRatioResult}.
Limits: the exact methods (`"midp"`, `"fisher"`) need the support of x11 given the margins (min(x11, x22) +
min(x12, x21) + 1 values) to be at most 2^23 (about 6 s), and `"fisher"` counts of at most 2^31 - 1 (as
`fisherTest`); the p-values of every method need phyper within its 2^26 terms (counts up to about 1e12).

oddsRatio#@throws.en:
TypeError if the table is not 2 x 2; RangeError for negative or non-integer counts, a table of zeros, a
  level outside (0, 1), an unknown method, or a table beyond the limits above.

oddsRatio#summary.en:
Odds ratio of a 2 x 2 table with its confidence interval and three p-values of independence. Equivalent to
`epitools::oddsratio()` in R.

The table is in epitools' orientation: rows are the exposure (row 1 the reference level) and columns the outcome
(column 1 without the disease); the odds ratio x11 x22 / (x12 x21) is the same for the transposed table.

Methods (`method`): `"midp"` (the default, as epitools: the median-unbiased estimate and the mid-p exact interval
from Fisher's noncentral hypergeometric distribution of x11 given the margins), `"fisher"` (the conditional MLE and
the exact interval of {@link fisherTest}), `"wald"` (the sample odds ratio and Woolf's interval on the log scale;
as epitools, no zero-cell correction: a zero cell gives an estimate of 0 or Infinity and NaN for the limit that is
not defined) and `"score"` (the sample odds ratio and the score interval of epiR's `epi.2by2`, Miettinen-Nurminen
without the factor N/(N - 1)). The mid-p and score limits are the roots of their equations to the precision of the
doubles (epitools solves with uniroot's tolerance on [0, 1000] and fails beyond and for zero cells; epiR steps by
0.1%). With a zero cell the mid-p estimate and limits follow the conventions of exact2x2: 0 or Infinity at the end
of the support.

`pValue` has epitools' three p-values: the two-sided mid-p (twice the smaller one-sided mid-p value), Fisher's
exact test and Pearson's chi-squared without continuity correction (with R's warning "Chi-squared approximation may
be incorrect" where an expected count is below 5).

onewayTest(0)#@param g.en:
Group labels, parallel to `x` (or the options, when `x` is an array of samples).

There is also a formula form, `onewayTest("y ~ A + B", data, options)` (next overload).

onewayTest(0)#@param x.en: An array of samples, or one sample with group labels `g`.

onewayTest(0)#summary.en:
Test that several normal samples have equal means, without (default) or with the assumption of equal variances.
Equivalent to R's `oneway.test()`.

onewayTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

onewayTest(1)#summary.en:
One-way analysis of means from a formula and a data frame. As R's `oneway.test(formula, data)`:
`"y ~ A"` has one group per level of `A`; with several factors, `"y ~ A + B"`, the groups are the combinations of
their levels present in the data (R's `interaction()`, the first factor varying fastest). Only the variables of
the formula count: the rows where one of them is missing are dropped.

pearsonTest#summary.en:
Pearson chi-square test for normality, with classes of equal probability under the fitted normal distribution.
Equivalent to `nortest::pearson.test()` in R. `NaN` values are dropped.

poissonTest#@param x.en: Number of events, or `[count1, count2]` to compare two rates.

poissonTest#summary.en: Exact test of a Poisson rate, or comparison of two Poisson rates. Equivalent to R's `poisson.test()`.

propTest#@param n.en: Numbers of trials (omitted, and the options passed in its place, when `x` is a table).

propTest#@param x.en: Numbers of successes, or a table of rows `[successes, failures]`.

propTest#summary.en:
Test of equal or given proportions. Equivalent to R's `prop.test()`.

As R, `warnings` has "Chi-squared approximation may be incorrect" where an expected count of the table of successes
and failures (n p or n (1 - p), p the given or the pooled proportion) is below 5.

propTrendTest(0)#@param score.en:
Scores of the groups. Default `1, 2, ..., k`. A group with a NaN score is left out of the regression
  (as R's `lm` omits it), but its counts stay in the pooled proportion and the weights, as in R. Other scores must
  be finite, with at least two distinct values. With no events or only events (all proportions 0, or all 1) the test is not defined (an error, as in R).

propTrendTest(0)#summary.en:
Chi-squared test for trend in proportions. Equivalent to R's `prop.trend.test(x, n, score)`. The scores are the
third argument or the option `score` (giving both is a RangeError).

propTrendTest(1)#summary.en:
Chi-squared test for trend in proportions, with the scores in the options:
`propTrendTest(x, n, { score: [0, 1, 2, 4] })`.

quadeTest(0)#@param y.en:
Blocks as rows, treatments as columns. Rows with a missing value are dropped.

There is also a formula form, `quadeTest("y ~ w | b", data)` (next overload).

quadeTest(0)#summary.en: Quade test for an unreplicated complete block design. Equivalent to R's `quade.test()`. Takes a matrix.

quadeTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

quadeTest(1)#@param formula.en: `"y ~ w | b"` (one variable on each side of `|`).

quadeTest(1)#summary.en:
Quade test from a formula and a data frame. As R's `quade.test(formula, data)`: `"y ~ w | b"` with the
groups `w` and the blocks `b`. The rows where `y`, `w` or `b` is missing are dropped first; then every combination
of group and block must occur exactly once (else the error `not an unreplicated complete block design`).

setWarningHandler#@param handler.en: The function that receives the warnings, or `null` to stop passing them.

setWarningHandler#@throws.en: TypeError if `handler` is neither a function nor `null`.

setWarningHandler#summary.en:
Sets the function that receives R's warnings, and returns the one it replaces (`null` when there was none). Not an
R function. It plays the part of R's printing of warnings (and, by throwing, of `options(warn = 2)`).

Every test, model and fit returns R's warnings in its result's `warnings` whatever the handler. With a handler
set, each call of such a function (and `pivotLonger` without `onWarning`) also passes its warnings to the handler
once it has computed its result: each distinct warning once, in order, with the name of the function called (a
function that calls another, such as `pairwiseWilcoxTest`, passes the warnings once, under its own name). A fit's
warnings are passed once, when it is fitted (`lm`, `glm`, `aov`, `lmer`, ...): a function given a fit or a table
(`anova`, `aovSummary`, `Anova`, `glmSummary`, `etaSquared`, `lmerSummary`, ...) keeps them in its result's
`warnings` but passes only the warnings it adds. An error thrown by the handler propagates to the caller. By default
there is no handler and nothing is printed.

To print the warnings as R does, set `(message, source) => console.warn(source + ": " + message)`. A handler that
throws (`(message) => { throw new Error(message); }`) turns each warning into an error, as R's `options(warn = 2)`.

The handler is kept on `globalThis`, so it is one setting for every copy of the library loaded on a page.

sfTest#summary.en:
Shapiro-Francia test for normality. Equivalent to `nortest::sf.test()` in R. `NaN` values are dropped; the sample
size must be between 5 and 5000.

shapiroTest#summary.en:
Shapiro-Wilk test of normality. Equivalent to R's `shapiro.test()`. `NaN` values are dropped; the sample size must
be between 3 and 5000.

stuartMaxwellTest#@param table.en: A square table of counts as an array of rows.

stuartMaxwellTest#@returns.en: The test result, with `statisticName` `"chi-squared"`; see {@link StuartMaxwellTestResult}.

stuartMaxwellTest#@throws.en:
RangeError for a table that is not square with at least two rows, negative or non-finite counts, fewer
  than 2 categories left ("Too many equal marginals, cannot compute") and categories whose off-diagonal counts fall
  into unconnected groups (S is then singular).

stuartMaxwellTest#summary.en:
Stuart-Maxwell test of marginal homogeneity of a square table (paired classifications into the same categories).
Equivalent to `DescTools::StuartMaxwellTest()` in R. The degrees of freedom differ where categories are removed.

Categories with no counts off the diagonal (in their row and column) are removed. With the K categories left, `d`
the differences of the row and column sums of the first K - 1 and `S` their covariance (`S_ii = r_i + c_i - 2 x_ii`,
`S_ij = -(x_ij + x_ji)`), the statistic `d' S^-1 d` is chi-squared with K - 1 degrees of freedom (DescTools keeps the
original number of categories less 1). For a 2 x 2 table it is McNemar's statistic without correction.

tTest(0)#@example.en:
⟦code1⟧

There is also a formula form, `tTest("y ~ g", data, options)` (next overload).

tTest(0)#@param y.en:
Second sample for a two-sample or paired test. May be omitted, and the options
  passed in its place: `tTest(x, { mu: 1 })`.

tTest(0)#@returns.en: The test result, with `statisticName` `"t"`; see {@link TTestResult}.

tTest(0)#summary.en:
Student's t-test. Equivalent to R's `t.test()`.

Performs a one-sample, two-sample (Welch's by default, or pooled-variance with
`varEqual: true`) or paired t-test. `NaN` values are dropped. As in R, each sample needs 2
observations, except that with `varEqual: true` a two-sample test needs 1 in each and 3 in all; an
error is also thrown if the data are essentially constant.

tTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

tTest(1)#summary.en:
Student's t-test from a formula and a data frame. As R's `t.test(formula, data)`: `"y ~ g"` compares
the two levels of `g` (the first level is `x`; `estimateNames` and `nullValueName` name the levels, as in R),
`"y ~ 1"` is the one-sample test and `"Pair(a, b) ~ 1"` the paired test of `a` and `b` (the option `paired` is not
allowed). Only the variables of the formula count: the rows where one of them is missing are dropped.

tost#@throws.en:
RangeError for a margin that is not positive and finite or a level out of range; Error where tTest has
  too few observations or the data are essentially constant.

tost#summary.en:
Two one-sided t tests (TOST) of equivalence of two means. Equivalent to `equivalence::tost()` in R.

Equivalence, |mean(x) - mean(y)| < epsilon, is shown at level alpha = 1 - confLevel when both one-sided t tests of
H01: d <= -epsilon and H02: d >= epsilon reject; the p-value is the larger of their p-values and `confInt` the dual
1 - 2 alpha interval (90% for the default `confLevel` 0.95). The difference, standard error and degrees of freedom are
those of {@link tTest} (Welch's by default, pooled with `varEqual`, paired with `paired`), with tTest's checks and
errors. Used on 0/1 data it compares two proportions with a t approximation; for counts
{@link binomDiffEquivalenceTest} is the better test.

Unlike R, a level of 0.5 or less (`confLevel`) or of 0.5 or more (`alpha`) is an error (the interval would be empty),
and so is a margin that is not positive.

varTest(0)#@example.en:
⟦code1⟧

There is also a formula form, `varTest("y ~ g", data, options)` (next overload).

varTest(0)#summary.en:
F test that the variances of two normal samples have a given ratio. Equivalent to R's `var.test()`. `NaN` values
are dropped.

varTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

varTest(1)#summary.en:
F test of two variances from a formula and a data frame. As R's `var.test(formula, data)`: `"y ~ g"`
compares the two levels of `g` (the first level is `x`). Only the variables of the formula count: the rows where
one of them is missing are dropped.

wilcoxTest(0)#@example.en:
⟦code1⟧

There is also a formula form, `wilcoxTest("y ~ g", data, options)` (next overload).

wilcoxTest(0)#@param y.en:
Second sample for a two-sample or paired test. May be omitted, and the options
  passed in its place: `wilcoxTest(x, { mu: 1 })`.

wilcoxTest(0)#summary.en:
Wilcoxon signed rank and rank sum (Mann-Whitney) tests. Equivalent to R's `wilcox.test()`.

With one sample (or `paired: true`) performs the signed rank test; with two samples the
rank sum test. The choice between exact and normal-approximation p-values, the
Hodges-Lehmann estimates and the confidence intervals follow R 4.6: with ties or zeros the
exact test is the conditional test given the mid-ranks, and an exact interval reports the
confidence level it achieves. Only `NaN` is dropped; infinite values are kept and ranked (as
R actually does). Where R 4.6.2 is wrong, the one-sample conditional interval and small
two-sided normal p-values, see docs/differences-from-r.md.

wilcoxTest(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns (`null` or `NaN` for a missing value).

wilcoxTest(1)#summary.en:
Wilcoxon tests from a formula and a data frame. As R's `wilcox.test(formula, data)`: `"y ~ g"` is the
rank sum test of the two levels of `g` (the first level is `x`), `"y ~ 1"` the signed rank test and
`"Pair(a, b) ~ 1"` the paired test of `a` and `b` (the option `paired` is not allowed). Only the variables of the
formula count: the rows where one of them is missing are dropped.

zTest#summary.en:
z test for the mean of one sample, or the difference of the means of two, with known standard deviations.
Equivalent to `BSDA::z.test()` in R. The open end of a one-sided interval is ±Infinity here (NA in BSDA). `NaN`
values are dropped.
